source_text.body:
Research market ideas and option strategies with Claude
A finance user has Claude gather ideas on world events and related companies, uses a research agent to find supporting snippets, builds option strategies, and aggregates short-seller articles.
·
Mar 17, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
One commenter, a day/week trader, said they use Claude to generate broad market ideas from world events and then map those ideas to related companies. They also use Claude’s research agent to pull specific supporting snippets, gather short-seller articles into one place, and sketch option strategies around trades they already want to make; the person remains the one choosing what to pursue.
How it went
The only result they gave was their own claimed trading performance: 153.34% gains over the past six months. They did not share a step-by-step workflow, prompt examples, or any evidence that Claude directly executed trades.
Worth knowing
The useful catch is how thin the source is: it names idea generation, snippet-finding, article aggregation, and option-strategy drafting, but gives no prompts, tools beyond the research agent, or timing details.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Research how [a world event or theme, e.g. a trade dispute] could affect markets. List the companies most exposed, find sources that support or challenge each link, and gather recent articles from short sellers about those companies. Then outline 2 or 3 possible option strategies for [a ticker I'm watching], with the max loss, max gain and key assumptions for each. Finish with a one-page summary, and treat it as research only, not a recommendation.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1rkiamk/question_for_those_in_finance_how_do_you_use
